parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac32ax^{1/2}-12$. *M1 for an attempt at differentiation with at least one correct term; condone poor notation. Use the chain rule with $\frac{dx}{dt}=5$ and $x=9$: $\frac{dy}{dt}=\left(\frac32a\sqrt9-12\right)5$. DM1 for correct use with their derivative; condone missing brackets and errors in their working. $\frac{dy}{dt}=5\left(\frac92a-12\right)=\frac{45}{2}a-60$ (or $22.5a-60$, $\frac{45a-120}{2}$, or $\frac{15}{2}(3a-8)$). A1 OE simplified. Total: 3.

parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Set their two-term derivative, with at least one term correct, equal to zero at $x=\frac14$: $\frac32a\left(\frac14\right)^{1/2}-12=0$.
